exposure: TORCH infections (Toxoplasmosis, Rubella, Cytomegalovirus, Herpes simplex virus) seropositivity
cohort: The study included 109 antenatal women with a history of bad obstetric outcomes, selected from both outpatient and inpatient antenatal cases attending GMCH Nagpur.
finding: TORCH infections, particularly Rubella IgG and CMV IgG seropositivity, contribute substantially to adverse obstetric outcomes among women with bad obstetric history, including a higher rate of LSCS.
mod_finding: Rubella IgG and CMV IgG seropositivity were significantly associated with a higher rate of LSCS, while Toxoplasma and HSV IgG showed no significant association with the mode of delivery.
